#1307. New footage shows how goalkeeper in Spanish footballer's killer collision was fired-up in moments before 'reckless' tackle - as police probe medical team after opening homicide investigation

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and NATALIA PENZA

Published: 05:13 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:28 EDT, 4 November 2026

New footage has revealed the tense moments before goalkeeper Jesus Owono launched a 'reckless' tackle that led to the death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker De Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

A homicide squad has launched an investigation as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation, with police now also probing the medical response to the incident.

Now, new footage taken from the stands has revealed how a fired-up Owono behaved in the moments leading up to the devastating collision.

The video shows how Owono had made his way to the other end of the pitch to get involved in a confrontation following a red card for opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, before appearing to motion for him to make his way off the field of play.

Footage has revealed the heated build-up to the tackle that led to the death of Jesus de Miguel, which showed goalkeeper Jesus Owono arguing with his rival goalkeeper. (Source: X/Eldense_)

Fans have commented in Owono's involvement in an argument with opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, who was sent off in the closing stages of the match (Source: X/Eldense_)

Martin and Owono appeared to continue their argument as they exchanged gestures as the Tenerife shot-stopper departed the scene.

The footage then captured Owono's wild celebrations - in which he leapt into the air and punched his fist - as Andorra FC scored an 88th minute equaliser.

'Here you have the images prior to the action by goalkeeper Owono, in the parts where he's not in focus — in one of them, he's confronting and saying things to the rival goalkeeper, and in the other, celebrating the goal right in the face of the Tenerife stands,' one fan wrote.

'He's a repeat offender when it comes to this kind of behavior.'

Another said: 'There isn't anyone from those of us who were in the stadium who didn't agree with the opinion that the entry was reckless. That it was an assault. It's clear that he didn't want the final outcome, but it's also clear that it wasn't an isolated incident.'

'I'm right behind that goal! Owono was completely unhinged! He came all the way to the rival goal to confront Dani, the Tenerife goalkeeper, over Lautaro's red card, and started gesticulating wildly at Dani to get him off the field after being sent off! This guy was totally out of his mind,' a third posted.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

De Miguel died on Tuesday morning following a horrifying clash with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

Andorra FC defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected’ by the tragedy.

‘There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,’ Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

‘What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

‘First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch,' he said.

‘I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

‘In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether Jesus de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died yesterday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his second-division club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

Police investigating the death of CD Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel are probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono

Well-placed sources told local press overnight there were 'certain discrepancies within the reports, or potential inaccuracies when compared to other evidence in the case' such as video footage recorded and posted on social media.

Respected island newspaper El Dia said: 'Among the issues currently under investigation, which according to sources remained unresolved as of yesterday, is whether the medical team who rushed from the sidelines to the centre of the pitch carrying a stretcher, a spinal board, and an Automated External Defibrillator to attend to the player, acted with due diligence during the more than six minutes they spent on the pitch before placing him on the spinal board for transport to an ambulance, which was stationed at one of the stadium access gates on La Mutine Street.'

It added: 'Investigators are also looking into an even more striking question.

'After a Guedel airway, a curved, semi-rigid oropharyngeal tube, was inserted into the player's mouth following his loss of consciousness, to prevent his tongue from obstructing his airway, was he also provided with oxygen during the resuscitation efforts on the pitch, as is required by protocol?

'According to sources, efforts are still underway to gather all available evidence to determine whether De Miguel was administered oxygen, either via a bag-valve mask (Ambu bag) or a face mask connected to one of the oxygen cylinders kept pitchside at the stadium.

'Sources indicate that this remains unresolved, at least regarding the medical care provided on the field of play.

'Furthermore, footage of the player being transported on a spinal board suggests that oxygen was not being administered during that process.

'Additionally, during the evacuation from the centre of the pitch to the ambulance, the player was carried on a spinal board by individuals who were moving at a jog.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel outside the entrance to Tenerife's stadium

'The manner in which the patient was transported, which should never have been carried out in such a way, was highly dangerous to their physical well-being.'

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who has lived in Spain since he was eight, was red-carded for kneeing Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel in the chest near the halfway line late into stoppage time. The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

Tragic Jesus, whose partner Maria and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time yesterday morning he had died at a hospital in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz about 8am, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats'.

It said in a statement, after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened: 'Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats, and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, which occurred this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8am.

'There are no words of comfort, there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow.

'We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire 'tinerfeñismo' community, who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Owono is reportedly intending to apologise directly to de Miguel's family for his challenge and has made his social media private following abusive chants and messages he received (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Owono is reportedly seeking to apologise to Jesus de Miguel's family before making any kind of public statement.

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said yesterday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

Later today Jesus de Miguel's body is expected to be flown to the Spanish mainland so his funeral can take place in the town where his parents hail from.

The 30-year-old footballer's mum and dad travelled to Tenerife after being told about the severity of his injuries before confirmation this morning he had died in an island hospital.

They will now make the reverse trip to Madrid before travelling to Navahermosa in the province of Toledo 80 miles south-west of the Spanish capital which they have chosen as the place for the player's funeral.

Jesus's club revealed the location yesterday afternoon but said it was unable to say at this stage when exactly it would be.

Town hall officials in Navahermosa, which has a population of just over 3,500 inhabitants, said immediately after learning of the footballer's death: 'Since yesterday, we had held onto the hope that Jesus might overcome the toughest match of his life. However, we woke up today to the worst possible news.

'On behalf of the town hall, we wish to express our deepest sorrow at this tragic outcome. We want to extend all our love, support, and affection to his family, friends, and everyone who is feeling this loss today.

'There are no words that can ease such profound pain, but please know that we are by your side and that we share in your sadness.

'Jesus, you have always been, and will always remain, a source of pride for us.

'Today, with broken hearts, we must say goodbye, but we will hold onto your memory. Rest in peace.'

Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of Spain's Castilla-La Mancha region which includes Navahermosa and the province of Toledo where a train crash last Wednesday claimed the lives of 69 people, added in his own statement: 'I am at a loss for words; the passing of footballer Jesus de Miguel, while doing what he loved most and what he had fought so hard for, playing football, is heartbreaking news.

'My thoughts are with his family, who hail from the municipality of Navahermosa in the province of Toledo. My deepest condolences.'

The entire CD Tenerife squad will travel to Navahermosa to pay their last respects to their teammate.

Flags outside the town hall flew at half mast today.

The National Police in the island capital Santa Cruz has yet to release an official statement about its ongoing probe.

A minute's silence was held before Champions League matches in memory of De Miguel on Tuesday

But a force spokesman said yesterday evening: 'An investigation is underway into the circumstances surrounding the incident which led to Jesus de Miguel's death which is being conducted by the homicide unit.

'It has been opened because the death was not the result of natural causes and it will seek to determine whether in terms of the law, an involuntary manslaughter could have been committed.'

The report police draft as a result of their probe will be submitted to a local judge whose job it will be to decide whether to take the matter further.

A Canary Islands court source described the collision between the two footballers as 'an accidental collision on the playing field.'

But he added: 'Any death not resulting from natural causes, referred to as a 'forensic death,' whether due to an accident or other factors, automatically triggers a judicial investigation, which is the case here.'

Court officials said this morning they weren't able to comment on when they expected to receive the police report into the drama.

One said: 'At the moment the investigation is still in the hands of police who will submit their report to a court in Santa Cruz once officers have completed their work.'

#1306. Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

Jackson gifted another massive opportunity. This time, Buendia whips a curling cross into the box and Jackson escapes his marker. However, the summer signing directs a second unchallenged straight into the arms of the goalkeeper. Jackson could easily have a brace already.

Early chance for Jackson as McGinn floats a cross into the box, which the striker connects with, but his header is collected by Ostbo. Jackson was unchallenged and perhaps should have generated more power on the contact.

Out of possession, it seems that Joao Gomes is playing at right back, with Mings moving out to the left. With the ball, Pau Torres, Lindelof and Mings form a back three, allowing Joao Gomes to slot into midfield alongside Barkley. It looks like a very fluid system. We’ll be keeping an eye on how Joao Gomes gets on.

The visitors get us under way. Can Villa continue their unbeaten streak in the Champions League or will Viking spoil the party?

Prepared for more. https://t.co/6XuohSA55y

Villa and Viking both stride out on the pitch. The noise from the two sets of supporters and the Champions League anthem is deafening. What a fabulous setting for a game of European football.

Unai Emery has a not-so-secret weapon in the Aston Villa technical area tonight.

Villa’s set-piece coach, Pal Fjall, is a former Viking assistant coach.

If Aston Villa beat Viking tonight, they'll be the second fastest team to reach 20 European Cup/UEFA Champions League victories (in their 30th game), only behind Real Madrid (won 20 of first 29). After a summer of upheaval, Unai Emery has got his Villa team clicking once again. In this form, they'll be confident of securing another win. @DavidSegar_ looks at how Emery's turned their poor early-season form around ahead of tonight's clash. 🔗 https://t.co/wV6Mr6vLio

Aston Villa: Suzuki, Mbaye, Lindelof, Torres, Mings, Barkley, Joao Gomes, Alysson, McGinn, Buendia, Jackson.

Subs: Bizot, Wright, Cash, Harwood-Bellis, Kamara, Garnacho, Abraham, Maatsen, Bogarde, Goretzka, Hemmings.

Viking: Ostbo, Herman Haugen, Daland, Stensness, Heggheim, Askildsen, Bell, Moi, Christiansen, Botheim, Tripic.

Subs: Belko, Vevatne, Postema, Bjordal, Bassey, Cosic, Fuglestad, Auklend, Falchener, Kvia-Egeskog, Kristoffer Haugen, Hansen.

There is already a lot of noise from the 2,000 or so Viking FK supporters in the away end.

Last week the club marked their return to the Champions League by securing a famous 3-3 draw with heavyweights Bayern Munich. Viking had led 2-0 at half-time before rescuing a point in the last minute.

A first win of the campaign tonight would represent another huge shock.

Villa’s co-owner Nassef Sawiris is in the house tonight.

Sawiris was the main driver behind the appointment of Unai Emery almost four years ago. Worked out ok, hasn’t it?

Elsewhere in Europe this evening, Manchester United are currently 4-0 down against Cesc Fabregas’ Como. Nico Paz has starred with two goals and an assist. Could this spell the end of Michael Carrick’s tenure in charge of Man Utd? You can keep up with the action and post-match reaction here.

Speaking to the club’s official website in his match preview, the Aston Villa boss said: “Champions League, every team they are playing Champions League, they are because they deserve it and they are dangerous and they have their collective and individual issues or characteristics as a team.

“Viking, they drew against Bayern Munich last week, they lost against Stuttgart. They are with Bodø/Glimt in the league, first and second with the same points.

“Bodø/Glimt is a team successful the last years in Europe, performing well, getting good results, playing Champions League, beating important teams.

“So Viking now is a new team as well, with the with the capacity to draw against Bayern Munich, the capacity as well to compete against Stuttgart and to compete against us tomorrow.

“This is Champions League, and Champions League is very difficult. In Champions League, we have now six points, it’s something amazing, but very difficult, and to keep the same way we are is our challenge.

“It’s not only Champions League, because Europa League is very difficult, and Conference League is very difficult. Europe is always very difficult.

“This is the first respect. We are Champions League, and each team is, of course, very, very respectful for us.”

Ibrahim Mbaye has slowly been embedded into the first team picture at Aston Villa by Unai Emery following his big money to England in the summer. The 18-year-old was used off the bench against Newcastle and looked very likely with his blistering pace and trickery. Mbaye starts this evening and we will be keeping eye on him, given his star quality and talent.

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Aston Villa fairytale under Unai Emery was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, Villa were stepping into the unknown despite the arrival of ten new players.

We have all learned, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their Champions League campaign so far and are running into fine form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

This could be another magical season under their brilliant Basque manager, with an exciting and vibrant new team.

Arriving at our home with our boss 💪 https://t.co/Mhu4WYvw3t

Unai Emery has made four changes to the side that beat Newcastle. From back to front, Pau Torres replaces the injured Wan-Bissaka. In midfield, John McGinn and Ross Barkley come in for Boubacar Kamara and Johan Manzambi. The interesting switch sees Ibrahim Mbaye also start, with Matty Cash the final player to drop out, making the identity of Emery’s last defender a mystery.

Tonight's #UCL starting XI to face Viking 👊 https://t.co/QUpQk2vWUv

#UCL nights at home never get old... 😍 https://t.co/OelbY4BlQQ

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Champions League fixture as Aston Villa host Viking in the Midlands.

Villa made history in their previous home Champions League outing last week, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 to seal the club’s biggest-ever European win. This emphatic victory, coupled with the hard-fought 3-2 triumph over Club Brugge at the start of September, means that Unai Emery’s side have made a 100% winning start to the league phase. The well-deserved 1-0 Premier League victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Saturday evening has amplified the positivity, with Emery’s new-look squad beginning to meaningfully gel and now boast a five-match unbeaten streak across all competitions.

Prepared for another night on Europe's biggest stage ✨ https://t.co/oZYiIiGvRg

Despite their Viking’s lack of European pedigree, Villa should be wary of their Norwegian opponents, who secured an unforgettable 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Stavanger last time out in the Champions League. The hosts initially flew into a two-goal lead at the break, before a double from Harry Kane and a strike from Luiz Diaz hauled the Bavarians ahead. However, after Michael Olise was sent off, Herman Haugen’s 90th-minute headed equaliser rescued a thrilling draw to give Viking their European point this season following a 3-1 loss to Stuttgart on MD1. Domestically, the reigning champions of Norway are joint top of the Eliteserien with Bodo/Glimt and embroiled in a nailbiting title race with just seven games remaining.

Villa’s injury list includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi, who both picked up issues against Newcastle, as well as Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri. Still, the hosts possess more than enough quality to dismantle Viking, particularly with Nicolas Jackson, who has been in effective form recently and netted a brilliant brace against Fenerbahce.

We’ll bring you the latest updates and drama. Kick-off is at 20:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1305. Danny Dyer Would Let Jarrod Bowen Leave West Ham For Two Clubs

Jarrod Bowen has been nothing short of incredible since joining West Ham United from Hull City in January 2020. The Englishman has been an extremely loyal servant at the club, even after the Hammers were relegated from the Premier League and into the Championship.

Since his £22 million transfer six years ago, Bowen has netted 94 goals in over 297 appearances and has become the talisman at the London Stadium. His place in history is already sealed, after he netted a dramatic late winner in the UEFA Europa Conference League final in 2023.

That delicate chipped effort secured the east London club's first piece of major silverware since the 1980 FA Cup. Bowen hasn't just racked up strong achievements on the pitch, but he's gained family ties to West Ham off it, too.

It certainly makes leaving a lot more difficult. But given the continued struggles the Iron find themselves in, he may be tempted to go against his father-in-law's ideals in search for a career more attuned to his quality.

Bowen married into one of the most well-known east London families he possibly could've when he tied the knot with reality TV star Dani Dyer in 2025. Of course, that now means Bowen calls notorious actor Danny Dyer his father-in-law.

Dyer is a massive West Ham fan and has often spoken about his delight at the Hammers' captain now being part of his family. Adding to that, the entire Dyer clan live in east London, and Bowen would have to think hard about relocating.

There was one big player who stood out as the hardest for Danny Dyer...

Speaking to talkSPORT in 2025, The Football Factory star was quizzed over whether he'd accept the West Ham captain jumping ship to any other club. At first, he shut down the idea of an Arsenal move, saying: "He’s never going to do that. Why would he? What’s in it for him?"

The prospect of another cross-London switch was quickly denied, too. This time, Dyer ruled out Chelsea as a possible option: "Why would he go there?"

However, two teams did come up in the conversation that Dyer claimed he could 'suffer' seeing his son-in-law join. First was European giants, and possibly the biggest club in the world, Real Madrid: "Real Madrid? Yeah, for sure."

Interestingly, it appears only one Premier League club would leave Dyer 'over the moon' for Bowen. Manchester City were given as the other acceptable destination. Dyer said:

"Listen, it’s his career. City? I wouldn’t mind that, I’d suffer that.

"I’m not going to lie, it would hurt, but he’s a grown man and he makes his own decisions. It would obviously hurt, but of course I would be over the moon for him."

With West Ham suffering relegation under Nuno Espirito Santo in 2026, Bowen and his teammates had to face the reality that they would be lining up in the second-tier of English football. However, the winger has stayed loyal to the Irons so far, despite the demotion, and the subsequent poor form to start the new campaign.

However, there will continue to be no shortage of clubs interested in the forward, who can play across the frontline. Reports over the summer suggested London rivals Chelsea were among the front-runners to secure his signature.

The Blues would likely be another team on Dyer's no-list. But with Bowen having racked up 22 England caps, he will surely have a pick of the club he desires should he decide to part ways with the east London side.

#1304. Fabregas: ‘Como must play our football, not scared of Champions League’

Cesc Fabregas insists Como ‘must always play the football that got us here’ in the Champions League against RC Lens. ‘You see some teams who look scared and scrape a point.’

It kicks off at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis in Lens Agglo at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and FC Porto vs. Napoli on the Liveblog.

This is only the second ever away fixture in Como’s Champions League history, and so the pressure is on to do the job even on unfamiliar territory.

So far in this historic campaign, they have beaten both RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at the Stadio Sinigaglia, but lost 3-2 away to Feyenoord.

“Every game is different and obviously we want to win, so I pick the players who are most suitable at this moment, there are four or five who can make the difference off the bench too, so fitness levels were influential,” Fabregas told Sky Sport Italia about his starting XI.

“It doesn’t matter if we are home or away, each match is important, but there is a lovely atmosphere here and it’s a good experience for us.”

The injuries remain substantive, missing Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Jayden Addai, so Tasos Douvikas is the only available centre-forward, but Martin Baturina is rested.

“The lads seem fine, I spoke to them before leaving the hotel and it is a big opportunity for them. We’ve got to enjoy these moments. You see these teams who play so well domestically, then in the Champions League they look scared and scrape a point.

“We can win, we can lose, but we must always play the kind of football that got us here. That’s how we see it, because in our small world we must find the motivation to keep improving. We’ve been trying to create a clear identity for three years, whoever we play and wherever we play is not an alibi to forget out football.”

Como have won their last five competitive matches in a row, and have a huge fixture coming up this weekend in Serie A against Inter.

#1303. Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR–Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal–fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

(1) RuV initially attaches to cholesterol- and sphingomyelin-rich membrane domains, which are abundantly distributed on the target cell surface, through calcium ion-dependent interactions involving fusion loops within the E1 protein. (2) RuV subsequently binds to hNectin-4 at the cell surface via the E2E1 heterodimer, which (3) induces endocytosis of the virus–receptor complex. (4) pH-dependent conformational changes in the E1 protein within the acidic endosomal compartment trigger membrane fusion between the viral envelope and the endosomal membrane, facilitating the release of the nucleocapsid into the cytoplasm.

#1302. Allegri: ‘Spoke to De Bruyne, difficulty but not alibi for Napoli’

Max Allegri makes surprising changes as Napoli visit FC Porto in the Champions League, but is tight-lipped on Kevin De Bruyne’s role. ‘There are objective difficulties, but they mustn’t be alibis.’

It kicks off at the Estadio do Dragao in Porto at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and RC Lens vs. Como on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Partenopei had a rough start to the Champions League this season with defeats to Arsenal and Villarreal, but finally got off the mark by beating Bodo/Glimt 4-3 in a chaotic encounter at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

This is a tricky trip to Porto, where Francesco Farioli’s side have a perfect domestic record, yet lost all three European fixtures to Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

“Unfortunately, it’s a risk to start Noa Lang because he had strong cramp on Sunday, he played four games in a row, so I preferred to rest him today,” Allegri told Amazon Prime Video Italia.

“De Bruyne told me his ankle is fine, I spoke to him, so I put him in the starting XI.”

Where the Belgium international is playing is confusing, as it could be in support of lone striker Rasmus Hojlund, or in the deep playmaker role with Scott McTominay more advanced instead.

“We must be aware that in football there are periods where things don’t go well, we need to be calm, aware that we’ve got to do more, but it is up to us to turn things around,” noted Allegri.

“We have two more games to play before the break for international duty, hopefully we’ll recover a few players after that. I believe in football when you hold back by just a centimetre, something you might take for granted, it makes a difference and you are punished for that.

“The results prove it, especially in the Champions League, where we alternated results and performances, so it is a step up we need to make. An example is Bodo/Glimt, when we conceded too easily at the end, because goal difference is crucial in the Champions League with this format.

“It’s a matter of responsibility and understanding the moments of the match, which we also saw on Sunday against Juventus.”

The 2-0 defeat at Juventus over the weekend only added to the injury crisis, as Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Mathias Olivera were the latest absentees.

They join Stanislav Lobotka, Leonardo Spinazzola, Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Costantino Favasuli, David Neres and Alessandro Buongiorno on the treatment table, while Luca Marianucci is ineligible for this tournament.

“We have many players who were and are out for a long time, so we’ve got to try to make the results co-exist with the fitness levels of the players. There are some objective difficulties, but they mustn’t become alibis,” insisted Allegri.

“We cannot concede goals the way we did against Bodo/Glimt and Juve. We absolutely must do better. When you are not afraid of conceding a goal is when it becomes easier to let them in.”

#1301. Celtic legend Frank McAvennie forced to apologise after labelling star's decision to miss games following his father's death as 'woke nonsense'

Published: 07:06 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:29 EDT, 4 November 2026

Former Scotland forward Frank McAvennie has apologised after describing Auston Trusty’s extended absence following his father's death as 'woke nonsense'.

Trusty announced the death of his father Walt last month, with the United States' international sharing a touching tribute on Instagram.

The 28-year-old has since sat out matches against Celta Vigo, Hibernian, Dundee United and Falkirk.

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill, speaking prior to the match against Falkirk on Sunday, confirmed Trusty was still yet to return as he was 'celebrating the life of his dad'.

Celtic subsequently fell to a shock 2-0 defeat to Falkirk, with O'Neill's side having won just one of their four matches in Trusty's absence.

McAvennie, who scored 37 goals in 85 games across two spells with Celtic, questioned the length of Trusty's absence following the bereavement.

Auston Trusty announced the death of his father Walt in an emotional Instagram post last month. (Source: Instagram/austontrusty3)

Ex-Celtic forward Frank McAvennie has apologised after labelling Trusty's absence as 'woke' on his podcast as he claimed the defender had to 'get on with it'. (Source: Let Me Be Frank podcast)

Trusty thanked his father for his 'guidance and unwavering dedication to our family' on social media and stated he would 'spend my life trying to make you proud'. (Source: Instagram/austontrusty3)

'I've got every respect for that, but how long do you want off?' McAvennie said on his Let Me Be Frank Podcast.

'Martin says he's away to celebrate the life of his dad. Celebrate the life? You've got football. You're getting paid and we're in trouble. How long is it going to be?

'It’s the woke brigade now, isn’t it? It’s nonsense. My dad was the best man, the only man I looked up to when he died, but you’ve got to get on with it.'

McAvennie has since apologised after a backlash to his remarks, with the 66-year-old admitting 'I should have chosen my words more carefully.'

'I've seen some of the reaction to comments I made on the podcast about Auston's absence from football following the death of his father,' McAvennie said.

'I can understand why people feel my comments were insensitive, and looking back, I should have chosen my words more carefully.

'Everyone deals with grief differently, and I certainly meant no disrespect to Auston or his family.

'Celtic need the big man back, and that's what I was clumsily trying to say. I wish him and his family all the very best.'

Trusty has missed Celtic's last four matches following the death of his father last month

McAvennie was part of the Celtic side that won the Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup in the 1987-88 season. He scored both of Celtic's goals in a 2-1 victory over Dundee United in the cup final.

The forward also helped West Ham secure promotion in 1991 during the second of his two spells with the Hammers.

McAvennie sold medals he won to Celtic-supporting businessman Lord Willie Haughey in 2000, after facing financial difficulties having appeared in court in a drugs trial that year.

He was ultimately cleared in court of conspiring to deal £110,000 worth of amphetamines and ecstasy. McAvennie had pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine, his second such offence.

McAvennie avoided jail but he was given a two-year conditional discharge and ordered to pay costs.

A separate incident saw McAvennie receive a four-month suspended jail sentence in 2009 after he admitted to headbutting a 23-year-old man outside a bar on the Isle of Man following an altercation.

The former forward, who had admitted to making mistakes during his career and expressed regret over his use of cocaine during his career, had his medals returned to him by Haughey in 2017.

Despite their recent run of form, Celtic are currently four points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, although nearest rivals Rangers have a game in hand.

O'Neill's side are next in action in the Europa League on Thursday when they face Turkish side Besiktas.

Celtic have lost all three of the league phase matches in the competition so far this season.

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1299. Manna: ‘Napoli knew Badiashile was a risk, De Bruyne in more congenial role’

Napoli director Giovanni Manna hints Kevin De Bruyne is ‘playing in a position that is historically more congenial’ against FC Porto, while they ‘knew Benoit Badiashile was a risk’ from Chelsea.

It kicks off at the Estadio do Dragao in Porto at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and RC Lens vs. Como on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Partenopei have 10 players out of action between injury and ineligibility, leaving only three senior outfield players on the bench.

De Bruyne had also been a major doubt after limping off with an ankle sprain during the 2-0 Serie A defeat to Juventus on Sunday, but he is in the starting XI in what appears to be a more advanced role behind lone striker Rasmus Hojlund.

“Kevin is a top player, he has proved he can play anywhere. Tonight he is perhaps in a position that is historically more congenial, but he proved that he can do well as a playmaker in Serie A and the Champions League too,” replied Manna on Sky Sport Italia.

“Tonight’s formation is based on how many players are actually available, and we had to choose from there.”

De Bruyne had not disguised his irritation at being dropped into a deep playmaker role in recent weeks by coach Max Allegri, so this feels like a victory for the former Manchester City man.

“The Champions League is still long, we are in a delicate moment of the season, but it’s important to put in a strong performance and give our all.”

Napoli have had a series of injuries over the last three years, something that Antonio Conte was already complaining about and now carried on into Allegri’s reign.

“We’ve had a lot of traumatic injuries too, like Di Lorenzo last year and Lobotka this time,” insisted Manna.

“We knew that there were players like Badiashile who were a risk due to past problems, Buongiorno we were aware of, Anguissa had trouble last season and is recovering, David Neres had a relapse, these things can happen.

“It’s not an alibi, we are here and will play our game.”

The January transfer window could be an opportunity to bring in reinforcements, especially for their strikers, where Hojlund has been used practically non-stop.

“The only place where we’re lacking is in attack, as today we’ve got two strikers, plus Giovane and Vergara who can play there. Alisson Santos is someone we never really had this season, but he doesn’t have a long history of injuries, so it was a new development.”

#1298. The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals1,2. For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour–nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour–nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

Legends and additional references for Supplementary Tables 1–6.

Behaviour statistics. Summary information for all behavioural tests for each manipulation. Values are reported to 1 decimal place. Number of animals is reported as n. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). In cases in which a Benjamini–Hochberg correction was made for multiple comparisons, an adjusted P value (p′) is shown (where p′ = P × m/i, where i is rank and m is number of cohorts tested; Methods). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For self-stimulation, ‘presses’ means the number of inactive lever presses has been subtracted from the number of active lever presses. In flavour conditioning experiments in which mice began the test with >90% preference for one flavour, statistics are also provided (in parentheses) with these mice excluded. Permutation (perm.) tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n > 9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note: this means the lowest calculable P value is 1 × 10−5).

Dopamine imaging statistics. Summary information for all recordings of dopamine release in each brain region. Values are reported to 2 decimal places. Number of animals is reported as n. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For photometry traces, dF′/F′ means the dF/F values seen during sham infusion have been subtracted. For rise times, s′ means that the time is relative to approximate entry of liquid into the stomach. For fall times, s′ means that the time is relative to the end of the infusion. For peak times during licking, s′ means that the time is relative to the start of the first licking bout. The baseline is defined as the first 10 min of the recording for GI and post-GI measurements, or 0–20 s before the start of the first licking bout for oral measurements. Permutation tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n >9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note that this means the lowest calculable P value is 1 × 10−5).

Single-cell imaging statistics. Summary information for all 1- and 2-photon miniscope recordings. Values are reported to 2 decimal places. The number (n) of animals and number of cells are reported separately. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For rise times, s′ means that the time is relative to either the onset of the licking bout or to the approximate entry of liquid into the stomach. Population-weighted activity (pop-z) is calculated for a group of neurons (for example, activated or inhibited neurons) by multiplying activity by the fraction of neurons belonging to that group. Linear-mixed models (LME) treat mouse differences as both a fixed random effect and covariate (Methods). The relative contribution of mouse differences to total variance is reported by ICCs. Note that, for PCA, the number of PCs is equal to the number of cells. Permutation tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n > 9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note that this means that the lowest calculable P value for those tests is 1 × 10−5).

fMRI imaging statistics (n = 38). Activity from left and right BLA clusters binned every 2 min (20 min total), as shown in Extended Data Figs. 10f and 11n. For PET statistics, see ref. 56. Each of the ten time bins after glucose intake was contrasted against the baseline (2 min before glucose intake), representing the change in brain activity after glucose intake relative to the baseline. The contrast for the first effect was [ones(1,10)], and for the following contrasts [1], corresponding to the different time bins. The significance threshold was P < 0.05, FWE-corrected for multiple comparisons at the voxel level within the left or right BLA mask, respectively, with initial peak-level threshold set to P < 0.05 uncorrected.

Pseudorabies statistics. Regional labelling (load) was normalized to VTA load to control for injection efficiency. From the 1,328 annotated CCFv3 regions, only grey-matter areas were retained (372 total), with cortical layers collapsed into single structures. Regions smaller than 100 × 100 × 100 pixels were excluded to remove small nuclei with high variance from few labelled cells, yielding 131 analysed regions.

Brain connectivity tables. Connectivity matrices were generated manually, with each pair given a number indicating bidirectional projection strength from 0 (no known direct connection) to 5 (strongest projection known from this area). The connectivity strength between an area and itself was assigned a value of 5. For deciding what strength to assign a projection, large databases like the Allan Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas (ref. 1 of the Supplementary References) were preferred, supplemented by additional sources comprising reviews and anatomical tracing studies (refs. 2–32 of the Supplementary References).

#1297. 'Players run through brick walls for him': How Scott Parker will fix West Ham - Mark Noble's helping hand, why insiders believe he can shed defensive style... and where it all went wrong for 'distant' Nuno Espirito Santo

Published: 12:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 08:44 EDT, 4 November 2026

For a club that prides itself on playing the 'West Ham Way', it has long been impossible to decipher quite what that means these days.

Managers have come and gone with no one able to tell you what their West Ham team embodies. What was the identity under Julen Lopetegui? What was it under Graham Potter? And what, after more than a year in charge, was it under Nuno Espirito Santo? If anything, the longer it went on under Nuno, the more unclear it became.

There had long been concerns in the West Ham dressing room, and boardroom, about Nuno’s confusing tactics, unforgiving man-management and humdrum training sessions. Club insiders described him as distant.

Few can forget the time he played his full backs on the wrong side in a damaging defeat by Brentford and then sent his team out against Leeds with no recognised forward and Andy Irving in midfield.

It was little surprise to see Callum Wilson, the former Hammers striker who started on the bench in those games, liking the club’s Instagram post confirming Nuno had been sacked.

Nor to see current jettisoned midfielder Edson Alvarez do the same when he can’t get into the side despite EFL record signing Arne Engels and Divine Mukasa being overrun every week. And especially not to see the wife of goalkeeper Alphonse Areola, now playing second fiddle to Mads Hermansen, posting an Instagram story to the tune of So Long, Farewell from The Sound of Music.

There had long been concerns in the West Ham dressing room, and boardroom, about Nuno Espirito Santo’s tactics, man-management and training sessions

In Nuno's stead, West Ham have turned to former midfielder Scott Parker to get them out of the Championship

Former West Ham midfielder James Ward-Prowse, another who was bombed out under Nuno, could barely conceal his glee when asked last month after his Southampton side's win at the London Stadium whether it felt even better to get one over a manager who didn’t want you. ‘I’m not gonna lie,' he said, 'of course it does.’

Nuno’s fate is not expected to be mourned for long. West Ham’s supporters had already made their own views clear.

Spurred on by the travelling West Brom fans at the London Stadium on Saturday with their hearty rendition of ’You’re getting sacked in the morning’, the few Hammers left at the end of their 3-1 home defeat joined in.

Three days later, they got their wish. ‘Following a thorough review of the start to the Championship season, the board of directors believe a change is necessary at this time to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track,’ read the club statement.

Those expectations are to earn instant automatic promotion, considering West Ham have the most expensive squad in the division and kept hold of Jarrod Bowen after relegation. But they are eighth following those back-to-back defeats by Southampton and West Brom.

It was a surprise to many that Nuno kept his job after relegation. David Sullivan, the former majority shareholder, wanted to sack Nuno in the summer but his influence in the boardroom was fading amid the BBC Panorama expose into historic allegations about his behaviour, which he denies, that saw him stand down as joint-chair.

Daniel Kretinsky, now the man who makes the decisions, wanted to keep the ship steady but has realised a change is needed after their unimpressive start. He made the decision after a crunch meeting this week.

And, so, for their fourth permanent manager since they enjoyed European glory under David Moyes, the Hammers have turned to one of their own former players in Scott Parker, out of work since leaving Burnley in April.

Former West Ham midfielder James Ward-Prowse (centre), who was bombed out under Nuno, could barely conceal his glee after his Southampton side's win at the London Stadium

The club's expectations are to earn instant automatic promotion. But they are eighth following back-to-back defeats by Southampton and West Brom

He will be in charge for the Cardiff game on Wednesday night. They held talks with Parker in the summer and are believed to have done so again last week following the Southampton defeat.

Insiders say the club is acting with more ‘normality’ these days under the leadership of new chief executive Karim Virani, a stark change from the madcap chaos of recent years, and the appointment of Parker, a manager with a track record of getting teams promoted, feels like another step in that direction.

Parker has won three promotions with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, with the last coming after racking up 100 points in 2024-25.

And, perhaps even more importantly at a time when the club are still searching for an identity, the 46-year-old – who was named Hammer of the Year three times in a row from 2009 to 2011 – knows what it means to represent West Ham. ‘He knows the West Ham ethos,’ as one senior club source told me this morning.

It’s expected that Hammers legend Mark Noble, currently sporting director and in interim charge, will form part of Parker’s staff. The fans, at least, will have figures in the dugout they can feel connected to.

Parker’s first job will be instilling a resilience that typified his Burnley team. West Ham boast the best attack in the Championship with 33 goals, helped by pumping six past Wrexham and Lincoln, but they have the leakiest defence of any of its top 11 teams.

Eight of their 18 goals conceded have come inside the first 20 minutes and, so far this term, they have failed to win when conceding the first goal.

By contrast, Parker's sides have kept a clean sheet in nearly half of his Championship matches. Burnley kept 30 in their 2024-25 promotion campaign, conceding 16 times in 46 matches and never more than once in a game. West Ham have mustered four clean sheets in their 13 games thus far and have already let in 18.

The 46-year-old - who was named Hammer of the Year three times in a row from 2009 to 2011 - knows what it means to represent West Ham

He will get a helping hand from former team-mate Mark Noble (left), who is now sporting director

Parker is arguably the safest pair of hands West Ham could have placed their promotion hopes in. Those hoping to be freed from the turgid football of Nuno, however, may still be left disappointed.

Parker’s sides do have an identity but it’s one based firmly on being hard to beat. Those who followed Burnley under him say that if they scored even once, they knew they would likely win. ‘Dour but effective,’ was how one Burnley source put it.

Even though they ended the 2024-25 season as the third-highest scorers in the Championship, they ranked only 10th for number of shots and their expected goals (xG). Eight other teams had more touches in the opposition box.

For all the grumbles over his style, Parker’s players loved him. ‘They would run through brick walls for him,’ said one Burnley source. An unusual flurry of long, heartfelt messages from his players followed the decision to part ways.

Those players who had their noses put out of joint by Nuno have a chance to reignite their West Ham careers.

Areola won the player of the season award at Fulham after Parker brought him to the club on loan from Paris Saint-Germain. Noble previously told talkSPORT how much he ‘always respected and liked’ Alvarez as a midfielder.

There’s still a hope among senior figures that having better players at his disposal will allow Parker to play a more attractive style than during his Burnley days. Many who follow the Clarets credit him with being able to build such a resilient team after losing a host of his key players at the end of the transfer window.

The issue, of course, is what happens should Parker get West Ham back up. For all his brilliance at getting teams out of the Championship, his record at keeping them in the Premier League is equally dismal.

Alphonse Areola won the player of the season award at Fulham after Parker brought him to the club on loan from Paris Saint-Germain

Parker was sacked after just four games at Bournemouth in the 2022-23 season

Fulham and Burnley came straight back down, the latter after spending more than £100million in the summer, and he was sacked by Bournemouth just four games in after a 9-0 defeat by Liverpool and complaints his squad was ‘under-equipped’.

Parker has won 55 per cent of his matches as manager in the Championship but only 15 per cent of them in the Premier League. His points per game plummets from 1.95 in the second tier to 0.7 in the top flight.

West Ham and their supporters may well harbour reservations over how they might fare in the Premier League under Parker but, right now, are in no position to think that far ahead. They need to get there first and, more than a quarter of the way through the season, have shown little to suggest they will.

Forget the carnival of free-flowing football for now. After putting up with a circus for so long, a little sense of order might be West Ham’s way back.

#1296. Farioli: ‘A privilege and honour to share a touchline with Italian giant Allegri’

FC Porto coach Francesco Farioli insists it is ‘a privilege and source of pride to share the touchline’ with Max Allegri, as the Napoli boss is ‘one of the giants of Italian football.’

It kicks off at the Estadio do Dragao in Porto at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and RC Lens vs. Como on the Champions League Liveblog.

There are some big question marks over how the Partenopei are playing this evening, because they are decimated by nine injuries, plus the fact Luca Marianucci is ineligible for the Champions League.

Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Mathias Olivera, Stanislav Lobotka, Leonardo Spinazzola, Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Costantino Favasuli, David Neres and Alessandro Buongiorno are sidelined.

Kevin De Bruyne would seem to be in a more advanced role supporting lone centre-forward Rasmus Hojlund, with Antonio Vergara and Matteo Politano as wing-backs.

“With the number of injuries for both teams, there will certainly be some changes to adapt to the situation,” Farioli told Amazon Prime Video Italia.

“Seeing the players there, I think Napoli will play with three at the back, but the way they approach the wings and attack is what will make a big difference.

“If they play with two strikers or one centre-forward, that changes things. We prepared for every possible scenario, but an experienced coach like Allegri could well come up with something we haven’t predicted, so we’ve got to be ready to react.”

FC Porto are top of their domestic league with a 100 per cent record, yet have lost all three Champions League games this season against Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

“We are a young team, so we certainly lack experience,” added Farioli.

“If we could the number of Champions League appearances on the field today, there is a gap with Napoli. Our performances haven’t been bad, but we lacked the ability to read the moments of the games.

“What happens in both penalty areas is decisive, and we lacked something there, so we want to do better this evening and be more concentrated.”

Farioli is Italian, but has never been a coach in Italian football, making his career in Turkiye, the Netherlands and Portugal.

“I have a big responsibility representing an important club like FC Porto. More than a battle with an Italian team, my focus is on representing Porto in the Champions League.

“Allegri is one of the giants of Italian football, so it’s a privilege and a source of pride to share the touchline with a coach of this level.”
